topics.topic: snake shedding isn't about growth -- adult snakes still shed for mite removal and eye-cap health
topics.title: A Fully-Grown Snake Still Sheds Its Skin — Here's Why

beat_timings.text: Most people believe a snake sheds its skin to grow — but a fully-grown one that's basically stopped growing **still** does it every few months.
Skin can't stretch as a snake ages, so shedding it scrapes off **mites** and heals scars underneath.
Snakes have no eyelids — the eye cap sheds too, and a bad one can leave a snake **blind**.
Keepers check every shed for two intact eye caps — a missed one can cost real **eyesight**.
Growth was never the reason — it's skin **maintenance**, mites and eyesight included, growth just tags along free. Follow for the one your biology teacher skipped.

topics.topic: the 22-meter robot arm built so no human ever has to touch Fukushima's melted nuclear fuel
topics.title: The Robot Arm Built So No Human Ever Touches Fukushima's Melted Fuel

beat_timings.text: No human has ever touched Fukushima's melted nuclear fuel -- the radiation would kill you in under **30 seconds**, so engineers built a robot arm to do it instead.
In 2017, probes measured **530 sieverts** an hour inside the reactor -- fatal in seconds.
That arm is **22 meters** long, built from 18 separate joints instead of one rigid rod.
Those joints let it snake through narrow openings and bend around corners no person can walk up to and guide by hand -- an operator steers it by camera instead, from a shielded room.
After 13 years, its first retrieval in 2024 pulled out less than **a gram**. 880 tons remain.
Somewhere right now, a machine is doing a job specifically because no person could survive it. Follow for the next one.
